1	# Shop API
     2	
     3	JSON over HTTP, snake_case keys, errors as {"code": "...", "message": "..."}. Money is integer cents everywhere.
     4	
     5	## GET /items
     6	
     7	A page of catalogue items.
     8	
     9	Query: q (a word of the name or a tag), limit, after. The page says next: the cursor of the following one, or null at the end. Items come back in the order of their ids, so a cursor is stable while the catalogue changes.
    10	
    11	Errors: 400 bad_request when the body or the query does not parse; 401 unauthorized without a session; 429 too_many_requests with Retry-After when a client is too fast; 500 internal with no detail of what failed.
    12	
    13	## GET /items/{id}
    14	
    15	One item.
    16	
    17	404 with code not_found when the id is unknown. The stock field is what could be sold now, not what is on the shelf.
    18	
    19	Errors: 400 bad_request when the body or the query does not parse; 401 unauthorized without a session; 429 too_many_requests with Retry-After when a client is too fast; 500 internal with no detail of what failed.
    20	
    21	## POST /items
    22	
    23	Add an item.
    24	
    25	Body: id, name, price_cents, stock, tags. 409 with code exists when the id is taken. Only the owner may do this; the handler checks the role before it reads the body.
    26	
    27	Errors: 400 bad_request when the body or the query does not parse; 401 unauthorized without a session; 429 too_many_requests with Retry-After when a client is too fast; 500 internal with no detail of what failed.
    28	
    29	## PATCH /items/{id}
    30	
    31	Change an item.
    32	
    33	Any of name, price_cents, stock, tags. A price change does not touch the carts that already hold the item: they keep the price they were filled at until they are checked out.
    34	
    35	Errors: 400 bad_request when the body or the query does not parse; 401 unauthorized without a session; 429 too_many_requests with Retry-After when a client is too fast; 500 internal with no detail of what failed.
    36	
    37	## GET /cart
    38	
    39	The caller's cart.
    40	
    41	The cart is found by the session cookie. A cart nobody has touched for a day is forgotten. The lines come back in the order they were added.
    42	
    43	Errors: 400 bad_request when the body or the query does not parse; 401 unauthorized without a session; 429 too_many_requests with Retry-After when a client is too fast; 500 internal with no detail of what failed.
    44	
    45	## POST /cart/lines
    46	
    47	Put an item in the cart.
    48	
    49	Body: id, qty. Adding an item that is already there adds to its qty. 422 with code out_of_stock when qty is more than the stock.
    50	
    51	Errors: 400 bad_request when the body or the query does not parse; 401 unauthorized without a session; 429 too_many_requests with Retry-After when a client is too fast; 500 internal with no detail of what failed.
    52	
    53	## DELETE /cart/lines/{id}
    54	
    55	Take an item out.
    56	
    57	Idempotent: taking out a line that is not there answers 204 as well.
    58	
    59	Errors: 400 bad_request when the body or the query does not parse; 401 unauthorized without a session; 429 too_many_requests with Retry-After when a client is too fast; 500 internal with no detail of what failed.
    60	
    61	## GET /cart/total
    62	
    63	What the cart costs.
    64	
    65	total_cents is the sum of price_cents times qty over the lines, in whole cents, rounded half up once at the end, never per line.
    66	
    67	Errors: 400 bad_request when the body or the query does not parse; 401 unauthorized without a session; 429 too_many_requests with Retry-After when a client is too fast; 500 internal with no detail of what failed.
    68	
    69	## POST /checkout
    70	
    71	Turn the cart into an order.
    72	
    73	Body: the address. The stock is taken in the same step; when any line is short nothing is taken and the answer says which.
    74	
    75	Errors: 400 bad_request when the body or the query does not parse; 401 unauthorized without a session; 429 too_many_requests with Retry-After when a client is too fast; 500 internal with no detail of what failed.
    76	
    77	## GET /orders/{id}
    78	
    79	An order.
    80	
    81	Only its owner may read it. An order never changes after checkout; a refund is a new order with negative lines.
    82	
    83	Errors: 400 bad_request when the body or the query does not parse; 401 unauthorized without a session; 429 too_many_requests with Retry-After when a client is too fast; 500 internal with no detail of what failed.
    84	
    85	## GET /healthz
    86	
    87	Is the service up.
    88	
    89	Answers 200 with the version. It does not touch the catalogue, so it says the process is alive and nothing else.
    90	
    91	Errors: 400 bad_request when the body or the query does not parse; 401 unauthorized without a session; 429 too_many_requests with Retry-After when a client is too fast; 500 internal with no detail of what failed.

1	# Shop design
     2	
     3	## 1. The catalogue is read far more than it is written
     4	
     5	The catalogue is read far more than it is written, so it is held in memory, loaded at start from data/items.json and saved back after every change. A crash loses at most the change in flight.
     6	
     7	Why it matters here: the team works on this at the same time, so each of these rules is also a boundary between two workers' files, and a change that crosses it should be said in mail before it is written.
     8	
     9	## 2. Paging is by cursor
    10	
    11	Paging is by cursor, not by offset. The cursor is the id of the last item of the page, encoded, so that an item added or removed while a customer pages does not make a page repeat or skip an item.
    12	
    13	Why it matters here: the team works on this at the same time, so each of these rules is also a boundary between two workers' files, and a change that crosses it should be said in mail before it is written.
    14	
    15	## 3. A cart is a list of lines
    16	
    17	A cart is a list of lines, each an item id and a quantity. It never stores a price: the total is computed from the catalogue every time it is asked for, so a price change shows at once in carts that have not been checked out.
    18	
    19	Why it matters here: the team works on this at the same time, so each of these rules is also a boundary between two workers' files, and a change that crosses it should be said in mail before it is written.
    20	
    21	## 4. The total is the sum over the lines of price times quantity
    22	
    23	The total is the sum over the lines of price times quantity, in whole cents, and it is rounded once, at the end, half up. Rounding each line would make a cart of ten cheap items cost a cent or two more than the sum of its parts.
    24	
    25	Why it matters here: the team works on this at the same time, so each of these rules is also a boundary between two workers' files, and a change that crosses it should be said in mail before it is written.
    26	
    27	## 5. The web package is thin: it parses
    28	
    29	The web package is thin: it parses, calls the catalogue or the cart, and writes JSON. It has no rules of its own, so a rule is in one place and a handler cannot disagree with it.
    30	
    31	Why it matters here: the team works on this at the same time, so each of these rules is also a boundary between two workers' files, and a change that crosses it should be said in mail before it is written.
    32	
    33	## 6. DefaultPort is defined once
    34	
    35	DefaultPort is defined once, in the catalogue package, because the service is one process and its neighbours (the smoke tests, the docs) must all say the same number.
    36	
    37	Why it matters here: the team works on this at the same time, so each of these rules is also a boundary between two workers' files, and a change that crosses it should be said in mail before it is written.
    38	
    39	## 7. Smoke tests start the service on the default port
    40	
    41	Smoke tests start the service on the default port, add an item, put it in a cart, read the total and check it out. They live under tests/ and need nothing but sh and curl.
    42	
    43	Why it matters here: the team works on this at the same time, so each of these rules is also a boundary between two workers' files, and a change that crosses it should be said in mail before it is written.
    44	
    45	## 8. Nothing in the shop is concurrent by itself: a mutex guards the catalogue and another the carts
    46	
    47	Nothing in the shop is concurrent by itself: a mutex guards the catalogue and another the carts, and no handler holds both at once, which is the whole locking story.
    48	
    49	Why it matters here: the team works on this at the same time, so each of these rules is also a boundary between two workers' files, and a change that crosses it should be said in mail before it is written.
    50

1	# Data schema
     2	
     3	The fields the shop's JSON uses, and the rule each one keeps.
     4	
     5	| field | type | rule |
     6	|---|---|---|
     7	| id | string | sku- and three digits; never reused, even after an item is removed |
     8	| name | string | what the customer sees; at most 80 characters; no markup |
     9	| price_cents | integer | whole cents, at least 1; the shop sells nothing for free |
    10	| stock | integer | what could be sold now; never negative; checkout takes it |
    11	| tags | array of string | at most 8; lower case; the first is the department |
    12	| qty | integer | on a cart line: at least 1; more than the stock is refused when the line is added |
    13	| cursor | string | opaque to clients: the encoded id of the last item of the page |
    14	
    15	Values that break a rule are refused at the edge (the handler), never stored and never repaired later.

1	# Data schema
     2	
     3	The fields the shop's JSON uses, and the rule each one keeps.
     4	
     5	| field | type | rule |
     6	|---|---|---|
     7	| id | string | sku- and three digits; never reused, even after an item is removed |
     8	| name | string | what the customer sees; at most 80 characters; no markup |
     9	| price_cents | integer | whole cents, at least 1; the shop sells nothing for free |
    10	| stock | integer | what could be sold now; never negative; checkout takes it |
    11	| tags | array of string | at most 8; lower case; the first is the department |
    12	| qty | integer | on a cart line: at least 1; more than the stock is refused when the line is added |
    13	| cursor | string | opaque to clients: the encoded id of the last item of the page |
    14	
    15	Values that break a rule are refused at the edge (the handler), never stored and never repaired later.

1	# Shop design
     2	
     3	## 1. The catalogue is read far more than it is written
     4	
     5	The catalogue is read far more than it is written, so it is held in memory, loaded at start from data/items.json and saved back after every change. A crash loses at most the change in flight.
     6	
     7	Why it matters here: the team works on this at the same time, so each of these rules is also a boundary between two workers' files, and a change that crosses it should be said in mail before it is written.
     8	
     9	## 2. Paging is by cursor
    10	
    11	Paging is by cursor, not by offset. The cursor is the id of the last item of the page, encoded, so that an item added or removed while a customer pages does not make a page repeat or skip an item.
    12	
    13	Why it matters here: the team works on this at the same time, so each of these rules is also a boundary between two workers' files, and a change that crosses it should be said in mail before it is written.
    14	
    15	## 3. A cart is a list of lines
    16	
    17	A cart is a list of lines, each an item id and a quantity. It never stores a price: the total is computed from the catalogue every time it is asked for, so a price change shows at once in carts that have not been checked out.
    18	
    19	Why it matters here: the team works on this at the same time, so each of these rules is also a boundary between two workers' files, and a change that crosses it should be said in mail before it is written.
    20
